subject: MAP: Performance benchmarks, TTFT & concurrency deliverables
messages:
From: Jordan Hayes <j.hayes@acme-robotics.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme-robotics.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff — performance targets and deliverables

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we discussed on the call, the executive team wants the mutual action plan (MAP) to include a clear performance evaluation section so they can greenlight the pilot. Specifically they want:

- TTFT (time-to-first-token) under our expected request mix
- 95th/99th latency percentiles for 1–8k seq lengths
- Throughput (tokens/sec and QPS) across target concurrency (1, 8, 32, 128)
- A CSV export of raw latency/token traces and distilled slides for the exec readout

Can you confirm you can deliver the slides + CSVs + dashboard link by EOD next Wednesday (2026-07-22)? Also include a short note on how concurrency was simulated and whether KV/prefix caching was enabled.

Procurement (cc'd) will want the same artifacts for legal review.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Hayes
Head of ML Engineering — Acme Robotics
j.hayes@acme-robotics.com
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Hayes <j.hayes@acme-robotics.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme-robotics.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — performance targets and deliverables

Hi Jordan — thanks, this is clear and aligns with what we planned for the MAP. High-level plan and owners below:

- Olga: MAP performance playbook & executive deck (deliverable: PDF deck + 1-page TL;DR) — due 2026-07-22 EOD
- Rishi: run benchmark matrix & deliver CSV exports (deliverable: per-run CSVs + distilled statistics) — deliver by 2026-07-21 noon PT
- Laura: Ops verification, Dashboard links and notes on environment (deliverable: dashboard share + run artifacts) — 2026-07-21 EOD

Benchmark matrix (summary):
- Sequence lengths: 512, 2k, 8k
- Concurrency levels: 1, 8, 32, 128
- Targets: TTFT < 120ms for typical prompt (512), 95th latency < 350ms for 2k, linear throughput scaling up to concurrency 32 where possible
- Modes: cold KV (first request) and warm KV (prefix caching enabled)

Notes about methodology:
- Rishi will use our dedicated test harness with fixed token distribution that mirrors your production mix (chat-heavy, median response ~48 tokens).
- All runs will be performed against the same model binary and quantization profile; we will record seq-length, tokens generated, per-token latency, and system metrics (GPU util/mem).

Attachments: RWD-Acme_MAP_PerfPlan_v1.xlsx (benchmark matrix, scripts, responsible owners)

I'll circulate the first CSV exports as soon as Rishi posts them. If Procure wants us to also include a signed attestation on test isolation, let us know and we can add a one-page note.

Best,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Hayes <j.hayes@acme-robotics.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 13:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — performance targets and deliverables

On Sun, Jul 19, 2026 at 11:02 AM Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com> wrote:
> Benchmark matrix (summary):
> - Sequence lengths: 512, 2k, 8k
> - Concurrency levels: 1, 8, 32, 128

Quick update — first pass results attached. Notes:

- Attached: ttft_concurrency_results.csv (per-request trace), perf_csv_export_20260721.zip (run-level exports)
- TTFT (median) observed: 512 seq = 98ms; 2k seq = 185ms; 8k seq = 520ms (cold)
- 95th latency (2k): 322ms (warm cache enabled), 410ms (cold)
- Throughput: linear up to concurrency 32 for our test harness; at concurrency 128 we observed tailing due to scheduler saturation on the test cluster (we captured system metrics)

Methodology details (short):
- Concurrency simulated with Redwood load-generator v2.1, fixed prompt seeds, token-generation capped at 128 for comparability
- KV/prefix caching: warm runs have prefix cache enabled and reuse for repeated sessions; cold runs are VM restarts between runs to flush caches
- All runs logged to CSV (timestamp, req_id, seq_len, ttf_token_ms, per_token_ms, gpu_util)

Next steps: I will distill to a one-pager of key numbers and attach an export-friendly CSV set for the deck. Laura, can you confirm the dashboard share link is public to Acme?

- Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Performance Engineer — Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
From: Eve Sims <eve.sims@alfatech-procurement.com>

Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — performance targets and deliverables

Thanks — the artifacts look good at a glance. A couple of procurement asks before we proceed to formal approval: 

1) For legal, we need the CSV exports and the deck as a single ZIP with a manifest (please include a short environment attestation).
2) Can you include the exact test cluster identifiers and the quantization profile used (we need it on record)?
3) Acme would like a 20–30 minute executive readout where Redwood presents the deck and answers Qs on the methodology. Availability: Thursday 2026-07-23 morning PT.

Jordan, Olga — please confirm ZIP delivery and confirm presenter for the exec readout.

Regards,
Eve Sims
Senior Procurement Manager — AlfaTech (on behalf of Acme Robotics)
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Hayes <j.hayes@acme-robotics.com>, Eve Sims <eve.sims@alfatech-procurement.com>

Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — performance targets and deliverables

Eve / Jordan — thanks. Deliverables and scheduling confirmed below: 

Deliverables (zip attached): perf_csv_export_20260721.zip contains: 
- acme_ttft_traces_20260721.csv (raw per-request traces)
- distilled_ttft_summary.csv (median/95/99 per-seq/concurrency)
- env_manifest.txt (cluster ids, model binary sha256, quant profile)
- acme_exec_readout_deck_v1.pdf (20 slides + appendix)

Presenter: Olga Petrov (I will lead the 25-minute exec readout; Rishi will join for Q&A on methodology).
Proposed slot: Thu 2026-07-23 09:00–09:30 PT — please confirm.

Notes for the readout deck:
- Slide 3: MAP context & success metrics (tie to your SLOs)
- Slides 6–9: TTFT & latency across seq lengths (includes warm vs cold comparisons)
- Slide 11: Concurrency scaling & bottleneck analysis (includes system metrics)
- Appendix: raw CSV link and run identifiers (we will attach env_manifest.txt in the ZIP)

Laura: dashboard link shared internally; please share external view to Jordan and Acme procurement by EOD.

Thanks all — we are on track to have a signed MAP after the readout if numbers meet expectations.

Best,
Olga

Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
